DEF-300.title: POST /api/analyze silently drops a non-object, non-array response body instead of reporting it as invalid
DEF-300.expected: Core's own validate() correctly rejects a bare JSON scalar (e.g. a number) as a BidResponse root with payload.invalid_root, status:invalid. The HTTP contract exposed by POST /api/analyze should surface the same rejection when a caller submits such a value as bidRes.
DEF-300.actual: Confirmed directly against the running server: posting {bidReq: <valid banner request>, bidRes: 42} returns HTTP 200 with validation.status:'clean' (only the request's own findings), and crosscheck:[] — the numeric response value is treated as though no response had been submitted at all, rather than being validated and rejected. Root cause: modules/analyze/handler.js:172 computes `hasRes = bidRes && typeof bidRes === 'object' && Object.keys(bidRes).length > 0`, which is false for a numeric bidRes, so validate(bidRes) is never even called for that side.
notes: The exact reviewed deviation is pinned per case and layer in knownGap.matches; unrelated failures are not admitted as this gap.

Distinct from DEF-115 (a crash in category traversal on non-array nested fields within an otherwise object-shaped, parsed response): this is a silent coercion of a non-container response root to 'absent', not a crash, and it affects the Core-vs-HTTP layer boundary specifically — Core's own validate() already gets this right when called directly.

DEF-301.title: A no-bid reason code outside both the canonical 0-17 list and the reserved 500+ exchange range is not distinguished from a real one
DEF-301.expected: Analogous to imp.video.protocols_unknown (Video.protocols values outside IAB List 5.8's 1-14 and the exchange-specific 500+ range get a WARNING), an nbr value outside the canonical 0-17 codes and the reserved 500+ exchange band should be distinguishable from a recognized code.
DEF-301.actual: The exact reviewed deviations are pinned separately for each case and layer in knownGap.matches; response.no_bid fires identically for every numeric nbr value regardless of whether it falls in the canonical range, the reserved exchange range, or neither.
notes: The exact reviewed deviation is pinned per case and layer in knownGap.matches; unrelated failures are not admitted as this gap.

mut-input-shape-nbr-exchange-specific is the positive control: nbr=700 (a valid exchange-specific code) must stay clean with no code-quality finding, confirming this gap is about a missing distinction, not about rejecting undefined codes outright.
